transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-24
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Claire Wong (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (BrightLayer ML Eng), Priya Reddy (BrightLayer ML Lead), Hannah Lee (BrightLayer Infra), Kevin Zhao (BrightLayer Product)

Summary: quick review of last week's INT8 run, FP8 baseline, small quality regressions on SQuAD-style eval, perf improvements in throughput and memory. Action items set at end.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this still the best time?
[00:06] Miguel (BrightLayer): Yeah works for us, thanks. we've got Priya and Hannah on too.
[00:12] Claire (Redwood SE): Cool. I'll share my screen in a sec, want to run through the updated numbers from last night's runs: INT8 and FP8 with our usual 8k context perf profile.
[00:23] Priya: Sounds good. our primary concern is P95 latency and any edge-case hallucinations.
[00:30] Claire: Right. Ok slide one, baseline FP16 numbers we ran on 80 tokens average, batch size 4 - single GPU: tokens/sec ~520, median latency 85ms per token, mem usage 38GB.
[00:45] Claire: INT8 run (post-calibration) gave tokens/sec ~930 (+~1.78x), median latency 56ms, peak memory 27GB. FP8 run appears similar to INT8 in throughput but slightly higher variance in latency  6 median ~60ms but P95 spikes at about 140ms on long prompts.
[01:03] Miguel: Wait, P95 at 140ms on FP8? that's concerning for our interactive use. Is that consistent?
[01:10] Claire: It's intermittent; we saw it on long prefix cases where KV cache misses and longer KV recompute happens. Could be spinner with attention kernels falling back. We suspect kernel selection fallback when quantization hits an unsupported op path.
[01:24] Samir: To add, we saw similar behavior in the small deep-dive last month  6 FP8 sometimes triggers a different matmul kernel on our driver, which has worse tail latency. We can pin a more stable kernel but it costs a little throughput.
[01:37] Priya: Quality-wise what changes did you observe? our acceptance criteria is <=1% drop on our primary SLA eval.
[01:44] Claire: On the current 500-example eval set: INT8 avg exact-match drop 0.6%, FP8 drop 0.9% on the core QA set, but we saw a small bump in hallucination rate  6 about +1.4% false assertions on the open-ended prompts for FP8. INT8 was cleaner overall.
[02:05] Miguel: hmm. those hallucinations are the main risk for us. Do you have examples?
[02:09] Claire: Yup, I pasted a few in the sheet. e.g., a probe that asks for regulatory limits, FP8 hallucinated an unsupported regulation number once. It's borderline but reproducible in 2/500 cases.
[02:22] Hannah: Are we certain those aren't prompt formatting or tokenizer mismatch?
[02:25] Claire: Good question. We double-checked tokenization; same tokenizer and the same pre-tokenized inputs. So likely numeric precision in softmax tails.
[02:34] Kevin: On infra, if INT8 reduces mem to 27GB we can pack more queries on one node; does Redwood support automatic packing right now?
[02:41] Samir: Yes, we've got continuous batching and packing. For Dedicated you can configure max-concurrent and Redwood will pack up to the configured GPU capacity  6 with INT8 you'll see ~1.6x to 1.8x cost savings in our estimates. Claire, can you confirm the cost delta?
[02:53] Claire: We're estimating unit cost reduction ~42% vs FP16 on the same instance type, factoring in throughput and effective GPU utilization. That's raw, doesn't account for increased ops for fallback kernels.
[03:05] Priya: Ok that's promising. For risk management, can we do a canary: start with INT8 for low-risk routes and fallback to FP16/FP8 when QA triggers?
[03:13] Claire: Absolutely, Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback by quality gate or latency threshold. We can push a canary traffic split.
[03:20] Miguel: About the evaluation size  6 500 examples feels small. can we run a 2k eval to be confident?
[03:25] Samir: That's on the agenda. Claire will run 2k with the same rubric and push to the sheet.
[03:31] Claire: I'll kick that off after the call, but note the run may take a few hours depending on concurrency. I'll also include per-prompt diffs and the raw logits for failures so you can triage.
[03:41] Priya: Great. For security, Hannah requested a list of ops that changed in the quantized graph and any new libs/drivers used.
[03:48] Claire: We'll export the quantization profile and list of fused kernels; we'll also include a short SBOM and note driver versions. That should be part of the security package.
[03:57] Hannah: Also need to know whether any plaintext prompt material is stored in logs and for how long. retention policy?
[04:03] Samir: On Hosted we have configurable retention; for Dedicated/Private you control logs. For this POC we set logs to 30 days but can mask prompts on ingestion; we'll share specifics in the security doc.
[04:14] Miguel: Any benchmarks on throughput when we enable prefix caching (we use long shared prefixes in our product)?
[04:20] Claire: With prefix/KV caching on, INT8 improves throughput further  6 we measured ~1.95x vs FP16 for short incremental queries because you avoid recomputing early layers. But FP8 had more P95 variance when cache misses occur.
[04:34] Kevin: Do you have example tradeoffs when cache size is constrained?
[04:37] Claire: If KV cache capacity is low you'll see more evictions; that causes rewarm which can hit the fallback kernels and spike latency. A mitigation is to bump KV cache memory or pin model layers that are hot. We'll recommend a cache budget based on your 95th percentile context length.
[04:51] Priya: About acceptance criteria, as a team we need to decide: is 1% drop OK or do we want 0.5%?
[04:58] Miguel: We should keep <=0.75% for core QA. If we see >0.75% we'll not push to prod.
[05:03] Samir: Noted, Miguel. We'll aim for that. Claire, can you highlight the failure modes in the CC for the 2k run?
[05:09] Claire: Yes, I'll include a failure-mode tag and a small reproduction harness for each failing prompt.
[05:15] Priya: Also include the exact seed and model weights you used so we can reproduce in our infra if needed.
[05:20] Claire: Will do.
[05:22] Miguel: Any vendor lock or proprietary tech in the quant path we need to be aware of?
[05:26] Samir: No proprietary runtime required. For FP8 we used a Redwood experimental path that relies on a specific driver matmul kernel; we'll flag it and you can choose whether to enable FP8 in Dedicated. INT8 uses more common quant ops and is more portable.
[05:41] Priya: Good. On timing, if we get the 2k eval by July 1 and it's within the 0.75% threshold, can we pilot INT8 for non-critical traffic in mid-July?
[05:52] Samir: That timeline is feasible. Claire, any blockers?
[05:55] Claire: No blockers. I'll need the eval list and some of the longer prompt seeds from your side to include in the run.
[06:02] Miguel: We'll share those by Friday.
[06:06] Samir: Ok quick recap of next steps then. I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and a link to the raw logs. Claire will run the 2k eval and share results plus per-prompt diffs and logits. Redwood will provide quant profile and ops list for security review. Customer to confirm final acceptance threshold (<=0.75%).
[06:24] Kevin: Thanks everyone. One last Q: pricing impact  6 does Redwood bill per token still the same way with quantization?
[06:31] Samir: We bill based on effective tokens and instance usage; quantization reduces effective unit cost because you need fewer GPU minutes per token. We'll include an updated cost sheet in the benchmark file.
[06:40] Priya: Perfect. Thanks.
[06:42] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.
[06:45] End of call.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts, some product names and kernel names abbreviated. Links referenced in the meeting: benchmark spreadsheet (drive link), security package (placeholder link), reproduction harness (git link).
